appDir.description: Absolute path of the folder that holds the web app. The page may load only files inside it.

page.description: The page to open, relative to appDir. Default: index.html

clicks.description: CSS selectors to click, in order, after the page has loaded (searched in the page and its frames). Optional. Runs before steps.

steps.description: A script to drive the page with, in order. Each entry names exactly one action: {"click": selector} · {"fill": selector, "value": text} · {"check": selector} · {"uncheck": selector} · {"select": selector, "value": option} · {"wait": milliseconds} · {"reload": true} · {"expectText": text} · {"expectNoText": text} · {"expectValue": selector, "value": text} (a checkbox reads "true" or "false"). A failed step is reported and the script goes on. To check that a page saves: change something (and press its connect/save control, if it has one), reload, and expect the change to still be there.

saveFolder.description: How the page saves. "origin" = the page saves by PUT to its own address (fetch('<file>', { method: 'PUT', headers: { 'X-Local-Origin': '1' }, body })), which is how an app saves on a Filer folder: the check serves the app from a throwaway local origin, keeps every save aside (nothing is written to disk), lists them (puts) and any the real origin would refuse (refusedPuts, with the reason), and serves them back so a reload step shows whether the save worked. "app" / "other" are for a page that saves with the browser's folder picker (showDirectoryPicker): there is no person to pick a folder, so the check hands the page one — "app" = the app's own folder, "other" = an empty folder that is not the app's, to see that the page refuses it.
